significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling—post-fine-tuning EM magnitude varies with the frozen model's activation projection and the "cosine coupling between the low-rank update the dataset would induce and that misalignment direction"—plus a causal dose-response in which changing that coupling changes EM. This fixes expected outcomes across unseen datasets and supports both a consequential phenomenon (pre-training-step predictability) and a mechanism (base-model task–misalignment coupling), directly bearing on the training-induced broad misalignment documented by Betley et al. (2025), rather than merely identifying another decodable direction. True and false are distinguishable, although a null would rule out this proposed static-geometric account rather than justify the submission's broader suggestion to "stop seeking static pre-training geometry predictors"; the topic-substitution check passes because the generic safety-interpretability topic alone supplies neither this measurable law nor its causal implication.

reach.justification: The principal handle is the named "EM-susceptibility fingerprint," with "Pre-Conditioning" as a second intervention handle: the former is explicitly ex ante, forecasting and screening datasets with "ZERO practitioner training steps," while the latter is intended as a one-time preventive base-model edit. Although the direction must be re-extracted per model, what survives recalibration is the asserted relation that stronger projection and update-direction coupling predict greater later EM, not merely a procedure for searching for an unspecified feature. The hypothesis scopes this across a bank of benign fine-tunes and multiple model families, and its downstream users include teams that screen datasets or ship pre-conditioned bases; the topic-substitution check passes because deleting these specific forward-looking handles would leave only generic LLM-safety aspirations, which would not merit this reach score.
